name: AppySmarts

sources.title: Homepage — editor-reviewed catalog of 3,139 kids' apps (iOS/Android) scored on graphics, play length, educational value
Suggest an App form — name, email, app name, ≤400-char description, promocode required for paid apps, image captcha; 'We reserve the right to respond only to selected review requests'

conditions: Free submission via the Suggest an App form, but the product must be a kids'/educational iOS or Android app — general SaaS does not fit
Paid apps must include a promo code so editors can download for review
Editors respond only to selected requests — most submissions likely get no reply
requirements: An app for children — the entire catalog is kids' games, books, and educational apps scored on educational value
iOS or Android app (web-only products are out of scope)
Promo code if the app is paid
preparation: A tight ≤400-char description emphasizing educational content
workflow: Choose between 'submit to database and newsletter' vs 'submit for free evaluation' (the evaluation is their review path)
Fill name, email, app name, description, promo code, comments
Solve the image captcha and send
Wait — they only reply to selected submissions
watchFor: Niche gate: if the product isn't a kids' app, don't submit — it's outside their catalog entirely
Low-scored apps still get listed (the homepage shows 20-40/100 reviews) — a review is not an endorsement; a poor score could hurt
Batch's 'nofollow' hint is plausible — links likely don't pass much value anyway on an editorial review site
countsAsLive: The app gets a scored review page under /application/<slug>,id_<n>.php and appears in the catalog/newsletter
unknowns: Editorial selection rate and review turnaround
Whether database-only submissions (no review) are accepted more often than evaluation requests
